newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia's Dairy Farmers Group not to list.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia's Dairy Farmers Group not to list.

text.p: Australian dairy co-operative, The Dairy Farmers Group, said on Tuesday it would never list on the Australian Stock Exchange as it did not want to dilute in any way farmer control and ownership of the group.
"We will not list," Dairy Farmers group chairman Ian Langdon told reporters.
Langdon said the group had other sources for capital injection, including through farmers themselves via high levels of retained earnings.

"There are a number of options that are simply not on the table -- we will not list," he said. "We will not do anything that destroys the cooperative status of the organisation and the farmer control that goes with it."

Langdon said the group would look at innovative ways of raising funds, but that listing was not one of them, as the listings of other cooperative bodies other had eventually led to the loss of farmer control.
"We have a very healthy ongoing injection of capital funds from the farmers and our retention policy reinforces that."
Earlier, the group posted a net profit for the year to June 30 of A$24.21 million, up from from A$22.83 million a year earlier.
Operating profit before tax rose 13 percent to A$30.08 million from A$26.54 million a year ago, based on a 16 percent increase in revenues to A$636.63 million.

The New South Wales-based group said it had increased manufacturing milk payments to its members by 34 percent to a total of A$83.0 million in the latest year. These are the equivalent of dividends for the cooperative members.
Dairy Farmers said it expected annualised revenues to grow to over A$1 billion because of its merger in March with Queensland dairy cooperative QUD.
The Dairy Farmers group is a competitor of the listed milk-based drink product companies National Foods Ltd and QUF Industries Ltd.
Dairy Farmers Managing Director Alan Tooth said the company's dairy food exports to Asia in particular had grown sharply in recent years and were expected to continue to grow.
"We'd expect our export revenues to triple to A$60 million this year," Tooth said.
Finding enough milk to supply this growth would be a challenge for the group, he said.
Dairy Farmers was currently in negotiations to merge with the Malanda dairy cooperative in North Queensland.
Malanda has 215 farmers producing 120 million litres of milk annually and had annual revenues of A$80 million.
Tooth said the impending deregulations of the New South Wales and Queensland fresh milk markets, due by January 1, 1999, would increase competition, but may improve margins.
He said margins in the Victorian market, which had already been deregulated, were actually higher than in New South Wales.

"I'm encouraged that the margins would appear to be higher in a deregulated market than in a regulated market," he said, adding that the deregulated market allowed more branding and value-added products with better margins.
